title: tte_pace
description: Time to exhaustion at a pace the CALLER names, the critical-speed twin of `tte`: S(t) = D′/t + CS, so D′ lasts D′ / (speed − CS) seconds above CS. The fit is the one `pace-curve 90 <sport>` prints: the grade-adjusted 5/10/20-minute speed bests of ONE exact sport (`sport`, matched case-insensitively, never pooled across a family) over `window_days`, today INCLUDED. `pace_s` is the named pace in seconds per `pace_unit` (one of `/km`, `/mi`, `/100m`, `/500m`), `speed` the same in m/s, and `cs_pace_s` is CS as seconds per `pace_unit`; `cs` is m/s and `d_prime` metres. `status` is `in_model` (2-20 minutes, where the two-parameter model holds), `outside_model` (real arithmetic the model overshoots on — read it as a direction) or `below_cs` (at or slower than CS the model says indefinitely, which is the model's answer and not the athlete's; `known` is false and `seconds` 0). `known` means only that the arithmetic ran. WEIGH THE FIT BEFORE THE NUMBER: `fit_r2` is the query-independent quality signal (1 by construction at two points, where `fit_points` is the signal instead); `contradicts_model` is true when the longest of the fit's own speed bests at or faster than `speed` (`demonstrated_s`/`demonstrated_speed`, in m/s) is LONGER than the prediction, so the model is refuted by its own inputs. `contradicts_model: false` is NOT evidence the fit is sound.
